_doc: T-3685: how the 1871 streets were surfaced, read from the Board of Public Works' Tenth Annual Report (year to 31 March 1871; source chicago_public_works_1871). Read by generators/city_1871_emit.py. 'stretches' are the streets the report names as wooden-block paved, each between two cross streets, with the page; 'totals' are the report's own mileage by kind and division, which bound the reconstruction (L-1871-street-surfaces): the report does not list the 37 miles laid before April 1870 by name, so those are drawn on the principal thoroughfares, as the Board says it chose them, until each division's wooden-block mileage is reached. Boulder pavement (21,150 lineal feet, nearly all in the South Division) is drawn on the river streets. Every other street is dirt.

note_on_reading: The warrant table is read from the Internet Archive's OCR text of the scan (archive.org annualreportboa06workgoog); street, from and to are as the OCR prints them, abbreviations kept. Stretches whose ends are lots, railways or parks, or which lie outside the drawn city, are recorded and not drawn (paving.unlocated in data/context/1871.json).

aliases._doc: Names the report uses for streets the 1871 network draws under another name (T-3684's crosswalk). Wells Street south of the river was renamed Fifth Avenue in 1870; the report's warrant still says Wells.
